## Selected work

The homepage lists eleven projects. The résumé picks six of them and adds Pops and Order Control, so all twelve are here. More experiments are on https://github.com/BiswasMosam.

### AMINAL

- What: Local-first voice assistant for Windows
- Year: 2026
- Stack: Python · Whisper · Ollama
- Link: https://github.com/BiswasMosam/Aminal-Public

Speech, LLM intent, vision and text-to-speech, all on-device: voice, vision and memory run on your own GPU and nothing leaves the machine. 29K lines of Python, 125 commands, 849 tests. An active project, still being extended. The source code is private; the public repository is a write-up of the architecture, capabilities, engineering notes and roadmap.

### Fill.ai

- What: AI form-filling Chrome extension
- Year: 2026
- Stack: JS · Chrome MV3 · LLMs
- Install page: https://www.mosambiswas.com/Fill.ai/
- Source: https://github.com/BiswasMosam/Fill.ai

Fills web forms from your résumé. It learns from what you type, handles Google Forms and Select2, and refuses to invent: every answer must cite a profile field, and one with no field behind it never reaches the page. A 92-check end-to-end suite guards it, and releases go out through CI/CD.

### Sim Sim

- What: Voice-driven AI desktop assistant
- Year: 2024
- Stack: Python · PySide6
- Link: https://github.com/BiswasMosam/SimSim-Virtual-Assistant

An AI desktop assistant you can talk to or type at: voice commands for the quick things, a conversational GUI for the rest. 70% faster task execution.

### Rail Mitra

- What: Railway platform and track optimizer
- Year: 2025
- Stack: Python · Google OR-Tools
- Link: https://github.com/BiswasMosam/RailMind

Assigns trains to platforms and tracks with constraint programming, so the schedule it hands back has zero conflicts in it.

### MindFirst

- What: Mental health screening platform
- Year: 2025
- Stack: Next.js · Flask · Prisma
- Link: https://github.com/BiswasMosam/Mind-First

Mental health pre-screening for 100+ students: a chatbot plus PHQ-9 and GAD-7 questionnaires at 95% accuracy, and 30% fewer people dropping off halfway.

### PixelForge

- What: Medical imaging with CNNs and GANs
- Year: 2025
- Stack: Python · PyTorch · GANs
- Link: https://github.com/BiswasMosam/PixelForge

Leukemia cell classification on the C-NMC dataset at 0.90 ROC-AUC and 95% recall. Labelled cells are scarce, so a custom spectral-norm GAN generates more.

### IntelliStatement

- What: LLM bank statement analyzer
- Year: 2025
- Stack: FastAPI · Streamlit · LLM
- Link: https://github.com/BiswasMosam/LLM-bank-statement-analyzer

Reads bank statements from PDFs and photos, pulls every transaction into structured data with an LLM, then charts where the money went.

### Committee Connect

- What: Android app for college committees
- Year: 2024
- Stack: Android · Java · Firebase
- Link: https://github.com/BiswasMosam/CommitteesManagement

A native Android app for running college committees, built by a team of four as a RAIT mini project, with Firebase Realtime Database for sync.

### PixelShift

- What: In-browser batch image converter
- Year: 2025
- Stack: Vanilla JS · Canvas
- Live: https://www.mosambiswas.com/PixelShift/

Drop in a batch of images and convert them all without anything being uploaded. It runs entirely in the browser.

### Flex Card

- What: Hardware spec card generator
- Year: 2024
- Stack: Python · PyQt5
- Link: https://github.com/BiswasMosam/Flex-Card

A Windows desktop app that scans your hardware and exports a polished PNG summary card, ready to share.

### To-Do

- What: Full-stack task boards with sign-in
- Year: 2024
- Stack: Node.js · JS
- Live: https://www.mosambiswas.com/To-Do/

Task boards with sign-in, from the Node backend to the front end. Small, but the whole loop.

### Pops and Order Control

- What: Two offline Android apps for real small businesses
- Year: 2026
- Stack: Flutter · Dart · SQLite
- Links: https://github.com/BiswasMosam/Pops and https://github.com/BiswasMosam/Order-Control

Pops is the order tracker for a fabrication firm, and Order Control is the order board for a food stall. Both work fully offline on relational SQLite.

## Research

### Comparative Analysis of Psychometric Data for Assessing Mental Health Testing Needs Using Machine Learning Models

- Role: Co-author
- Venue: IEEE Xplore · Proceedings of ICAIIHI 2025, the 2nd International Conference on AI for Innovations in Healthcare Industries
- Presented: December 2025, Paper ID 34, with a Certificate of Appreciation
- Paper: https://doi.ieeecomputersociety.org/10.1109/ICAIIHI67124.2025.11403838
- PDF: https://www.mosambiswas.com/ResearchPaper.pdf

Can supervised learning decide who should go on to a full mental health evaluation? The paper benchmarks Logistic Regression, Random Forest, SVM, XGBoost and LightGBM on 28.5K PHQ-9 / GAD-7 records, with stratified 5-fold cross-validation and paired t-tests. Logistic Regression led at 99% accuracy, with SHAP explanations that make each call transparent enough to be clinically meaningful, and the pre-screening flow roughly halves screening overhead.

## About this site

- Built by hand with no framework, no libraries and no build step: hand-written HTML, CSS and JavaScript.
- The smoke and embers in the background are a raw WebGL fragment shader.
- Installable as an offline app. A service worker precaches the whole site, résumé and type included, so it opens with no network.
- Type: Syne, Instrument Serif, Manrope and Space Mono, all self-hosted.
- Hosted on GitHub Pages. Source: https://github.com/BiswasMosam/BiswasMosam.github.io
- The bare domain runs Shellfolio, a small Go server (https://github.com/BiswasMosam/Shellfolio). In a terminal, `curl mosambiswas.com` prints the résumé and `ssh mosambiswas.com` opens the whole portfolio as a terminal app. Browsers are sent on to www.
- The site also hides a few easter eggs. They are left out of this file on purpose; https://www.mosambiswas.com/humans.txt has hints.
